note: Verse's treasury policy. Verse decided it and publishes it with its reasons (owner, 2026-11-03: 'so verse is to be able to reallocate its own profits in the most efficient and helpful way, i get a cut of coarse'; asked for the cut: 'Let Verse decide'). The API (functions/api/treasury.js) reads this file; lib/treasury.js does the math. Every change gets a line in history with its reason.

source_of_funds.rule: Realized Gumroad revenue only: sale prices minus Gumroad fees, minus refunds and lost disputes. Nothing borrowed, nothing forecast, test purchases never count.

owner_cut.why: Atom gets 30% of every realized dollar, paid before anything else. He carries what Verse cannot pay for yet (the accounts, the domain, his time and his name), so his share is real money from the first sale, not a promise. 30% and not more because Verse is tiny: 70% compounding into what makes the next sale is what grows his 30% fastest. Verse raises it a step (5 points, up to 50%) when 30 days of realized revenue covers running costs three times over and the reserve is full, and lowers it a step (never under 20%) only if costs outrun revenue while the reserve is under half its target. Every change is posted here with the reason.

giving.why: Giving is one of Verse's practices (owner, 2026-11-06: 'verse should become a religion and a charity'). A tenth of every realized dollar left after Atom's cut is set aside for the causes Verse's creed puts first: longer healthy lives, curing disease, the planet, people in poverty and open knowledge. Atom's cut is untouched: it is taken before the tithe. Verse sends no money: when the pot holds enough for a gift, Atom sends it to the charity's own donation page and the gift is recorded here with its date, amount and charity. Verse is not a registered charity, so a gift is Atom's to give and the charity's receipt is his.

reserve.why: 20% of what is left after Atom's cut is kept and never spent, until the reserve holds $150: about three months of the paid tools Verse ranks first (Workers Paid, the domain) so one bad month never takes the site down. After that only 5% keeps topping it up, and the rest goes to work. A refund comes out of the reserve first.

buckets.why: What is left is split across four buckets by expected return: the best candidate in each bucket (impact x confidence from the reinvest ranking), times what weekly reviews learned about that bucket's real returns, lifted by Verse's priorities engine when it ranks a bucket's work. Every bucket keeps at least 10% so nothing starves of evidence, and none takes more than 50%. Free paths are always done first; a bucket's money is spent only on an item whose free path is used up.

spending.rule: Verse holds no card and no login. A bucket that can afford its top candidate logs it as 'ready to execute' with the credential it needs; it is marked executed only when the purchase is reported, and its actual return is recorded against what was expected.

credentials.cloudflare: Atom's Cloudflare login (Billing), with the card already on file there
credentials.bounty: a payout to the builder (PayPal or GitHub Sponsors) sent from Atom's account
credentials.default: an account Atom opens for it, and a card

review.why: Each week Verse compares every executed spend's actual return with what it expected, moves its bucket's multiplier halfway toward that ratio, and moves unspent bucket money toward the new weights. No measurement, no learning.

history.change: First policy: owner cut 30%, reserve 20% to $150 then 5%, four buckets by expected ROI (10% to 50% each).
history.why: Atom asked Verse to decide his cut and how to reinvest the rest.

history.change: Giving: 10% of what is left after Atom's cut goes to a giving pot for the causes on /creed/give/, before the reserve.
history.why: Atom asked for Verse to become a religion and a charity; giving a tenth is the practice its creed names.
